subject: 2027 new-grad slate — committee approval and comp-band ask
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: 2027 new-grad slate — committee approval and comp-band ask

Team,

I ran the 2027 new-grad slate by the hiring leads this morning and we have a proposed allocation and recommended comp bands. High level: 8 total headcount across Engineering (4), Platform (2), and Product (2). We'd like to extend offers starting mid-July to lock campuses and avoid losing candidates to competitors.

Asks:
- Leadership headcount approval for 8 FTEs in Q3 (we can reduce to 6 if budget is constrained).
- Approve comp-band ranges for entry-level roles (L3 / New Grad): base + target equity band. See the attached comp-bands-proposal.pdf for suggested numbers.
- Signoff on the hire timing so Talent can begin offer templating and candidate outreach.

Attachments: 2027-new-grad-slate.xlsx (workload & role split), comp-bands-proposal.pdf (recommended ranges)

I copied Payroll and Hiring leads (Marissa) for visibility. If we want to trim to 6, propose removing one Product and one Platform role.

Thanks,
Karthik
--
Karthik Iyer
Director, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 10:03:22 -0700
Subject: Re: 2027 new-grad slate — committee approval and comp-band ask

Karthik,

Thanks for pulling this together — clear and actionable. A couple quick notes after a skim:
- Budget: current Q3 hiring envelope is tighter than we expected. I recommend we aim for 6 instead of 8 (remove one Platform, one Product) unless Markus confirms incremental funding.
- Comp bands: the ranges in comp-bands-proposal.pdf look market-competitive, but please include total OTE and an example offer for a high-priority candidate (base + bonus + equity).
- Can you add an estimated 12-month run rate impact (headcount cost + comp) in the spreadsheet? That helps Finance reconcile the forecast.

I added a short comment on the Drive doc (link below) and flagged for the Hiring Committee review tomorrow at 2pm.

Related link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-newgrad-slate

—Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, People Operations
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: 2027 new-grad slate — committee approval and comp-band ask

Thanks, everyone — quick decision so Talent can move: I approve moving forward with 6 hires (Engineering x4, Platform x1, Product x1) to stay within the Q3 envelope.

Comp bands (final, for offer templates):
- L3 Engineer: Base $110,000 — $125,000; target equity 0.05% — 0.08%; signing bonus allowed up to $5,000 for high-priority candidates.
- L3 Platform: Base $115,000 — $128,000; target equity 0.06% — 0.09%; signing bonus allowed up to $7,500.
- L3 Product: Base $100,000 — $115,000; RSU band 0.03% — 0.06%.

Please use mid-point offers for the initial batch and reserve stretching authority (+5–8% base or small signing bonus) for the top 2 candidates in each pool. Start window: July 18–29 (prefer the week of July 18).

Marissa — can you generate the 6 offer letters with the bands above and route to Payroll for run-rate estimate (Laura requested 12-month cost). Ben — once letters are ready, please book final candidate windows; we want verbal acceptances by June 15.

Attachments: none

Thanks,
Karthik

Karthik — good call trimming to 6. Approve the above comp bands and the proposed signing bonuses for market competitiveness. Two administrative asks from Finance before you finalize offers:
1) Add a one-time onboarding stipend line (recommended $1,500) for out-of-region hires and label it as a lump-sum reimbursement.
2) Tag the 6 hires to Q3 forecast with a headcount flag so our reporting reflects the incremental HC.

Once Marissa confirms the offer letters, I approve moving these through Payroll and Legal. If any exceptional counters come back, loop me in — we can approve stretch offers up to an additional $8k signing bonus on a case-by-case basis.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
VP, Finance
